## Evidence-first decisions

### Technical

The initial product/source review found no reproducible reader, documentation-rendering, crawlability, analytics-instrumentation, build, or maintained-source-output defect. After the first closeout merged, its post-merge Quality run exposed a release-gating reliability defect in the Chromium setup; that defect was repaired in the same operating cycle and is recorded below. Runtime analytics ownership remains the single GA4 destination `G-DGH8HNQKE4`; application and documentation output continue to require full `page_location` via `window.location.href` and query-bearing `page_path` via `window.location.pathname + window.location.search`, with Google signals and ad-personalization signals disabled. The production verifier and product assertions were not weakened.

The direct-TXT source added today relies on WebNR's existing explicit URL-import path rather than adding a proxy or a new ingestion runtime. The source index remains subject to the existing 5 MiB repository-index bound. A reader explicitly choosing a direct entry navigates through the existing `?add=` path to the exact HTTPS raw-text URL; WebNR does not add background synchronization, server-side fetching, credentials, cookies, or a crawler.

### Sources

The daily source program screened five new raw/open-text candidate families: Project Ben-Yehuda's `public_domain_dump`, Project Gutenberg Australia, Project Gutenberg Canada, GITenberg, and the Internet Sacred Text Archive.

Project Ben-Yehuda received the admitted integration. Its official GitHub organization publishes `public_domain_dump`; the audited upstream commit is `5e4277fead7b565f32cc4b352abd3565023a77d8`. The upstream README describes more than twenty thousand public-domain Hebrew works in plaintext UTF-8 and HTML and documents `pseudocatalogue.csv` metadata. The repository LICENSE states that the data files are in the public domain and may be used without permission, with optional credit to Project Ben-Yehuda volunteers. The audited dump paths and metadata were checked for four representative works: work 10 `חצי-נחמה`, work 28 `מעל מכסה האניה`, work 33 `הַתַּכְרִיך`, and work 40 `שני ימים ולילה אחד בבית מלון אורחים`. Their WebNR `download_url` values are pinned to the exact audited upstream commit, while Project Ben-Yehuda reader pages remain as human-readable provenance URLs.

This is intentionally a real direct-TXT source rather than another static link-only directory. WebNR still keeps the capability bounded: four version-pinned UTF-8 texts, no catalog mirroring, no background polling, no reader-page crawling, no accounts, and no cookies. Project Ben-Yehuda also documents an API, but that interface was not used because it requires an API key and carries a request-rate boundary. The public-domain dump gives this first integration a credential-free, reviewable snapshot identity.

Project Gutenberg Australia received a complete rights/access review and remains deferred for a global direct-TXT source. Its first-party license says most ebooks are public domain in Australia, some are redistributed by permission with additional restrictions, and people outside Australia must check their own national copyright law. The current catalog includes works that can be public domain in Australia while remaining copyrighted elsewhere. WebNR therefore did not convert an Australia-specific public-domain determination into a blanket global ingestion claim.

Project Gutenberg Canada received a complete rights/access review and remains deferred for the same jurisdiction-specific reason. Its first-party catalog states that the ebooks are in the Canadian public domain and explicitly tells users outside Canada to download only when the work is also public domain in their own country. A future integration would need a per-item jurisdiction-safe subset or a capability that does not imply globally safe redistribution.

GITenberg received a complete technical/value review. It exposes a large Git-backed collection of Project Gutenberg-derived public-domain books with standard metadata/license files and machine-friendly source repositories. It is technically attractive, but it substantially overlaps WebNR's existing Project Gutenberg discovery value; adding a second near-duplicate starter today would not improve reader coverage enough to justify another maintained source. It remains a possible transport/fallback candidate where a concrete non-duplicative benefit is proven.

The Internet Sacred Text Archive was screened and rights-reviewed but not blanket-admitted. Its first-party copyright documentation distinguishes public-domain material, ISTA-prepared texts with attribution/non-commercial conditions, copyrighted material released for limited redistribution, and site-original copyrighted content; the catalog itself warns that listing does not prove unrestricted copyright status. Any future direct source therefore requires item-level rights evidence rather than treating the archive as one homogeneous public-domain corpus.

Rotating health review rechecked three already maintained source families. Standard Ebooks' public work/catalog surface remained available; Wolne Lektury's catalog/public reading surface remained available with its current licensing/public-domain notices; Project Madurai's public Tamil etext/list surface remained available with its existing distribution boundary. No evidence justified removing or broadening any of those maintained sources in this cycle.

The daily target of screening at least five candidates, fully auditing at least three, shipping at least one passing integration, and rotating existing-source health was satisfied.

## Same-cycle release-gate repair — pull request #131

The first closeout pull request #130 completed the corrected four-job PR-head Quality workflow and exact-head squash merged as `d54f1f425ab787cabd7866b023b6e525edafd802`. Its subsequent main-branch Quality run `33417845290` preserved successful Web quality, Documentation quality, and Production evidence, but Chromium user journeys failed before browser execution in three attempts at the dynamic Playwright setup step. The first attempt hit an `ECONNRESET` while fetching the `canvas` prebuilt binary and then a native-build fallback without `pixman-1`; the next two attempts failed with npm registry `ETARGET` resolution errors for unrelated `@typescript-eslint/eslint-plugin@8.69.0` and `@typescript-eslint/visitor-keys@8.69.0`. Those failures occurred because `npm install --no-save --package-lock=false @playwright/test@1.62.0` ran in the repository root after `npm ci`, causing npm to re-resolve the application dependency graph against live registry state. No browser journey failed; the browser tests never started in those attempts.

Pull request #131 repaired that release-gating defect without weakening a product or production assertion. The pinned `@playwright/test@1.62.0` runner is now installed into an isolated temporary prefix with a clean directory and at most three bounded retries; only that isolated runner's executable directory and module path are exported for later Chromium/test steps. Application dependencies remain installed exclusively by the lockfile-backed `npm ci`. The final PR head `6b39a96f46208d7e5e57897cc5d913063b83e0e0` completed Quality run `33418600679` with Web quality, Documentation quality, Production evidence, and Chromium user journeys all successful; the isolated runner install, Chromium install, production build, and actual browser user journeys all executed successfully. After the required fresh one-file review, #131 exact-head squash merged as `8e59cf00b85cefe63a6c8404177b9282fa096e03`.

The post-merge main-branch Quality run `33418849715` then completed all four jobs successfully on the repaired workflow. Chromium user journeys independently completed the isolated Playwright install, Chromium installation, production application build, and actual browser test execution. Its Production evidence job observed application `61251824a3bef5fa334f7de4b76d5104de5f7711`, documentation mirror `cfc4df017a03506cbb9415feec36ab132bff398f`, and canonical documentation `61251824a3bef5fa334f7de4b76d5104de5f7711` at approximately 2026-08-31T17:18:40Z.

The canonical Cloudflare documentation project then completed its normal asynchronous rebuild from #131. The first Quality run on closeout pull request #132, run `33419199528`, independently observed `https://www.webnovel.win/build.json` reporting exact source commit `8e59cf00b85cefe63a6c8404177b9282fa096e03`, `source: cloudflare-pages`, and `builtAt: 2026-08-31T17:21:45.648786+00:00` on all 42 Production evidence retries. In that same run the application still verified as `61251824a3bef5fa334f7de4b76d5104de5f7711`, the documentation mirror still verified as `cfc4df017a03506cbb9415feec36ab132bff398f`, and Web quality, Documentation quality, and Chromium user journeys all succeeded. Production evidence failed only because the closeout metadata still expected the pre-rebuild canonical identity. This is a second truthful production-identity drift signal, not a verifier or rendered-site regression.
